author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Conservationists are monitoring twin light beams projected from the Mount Washington summit for the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks, watching for signs that migrating birds are becoming disoriented.

New Hampshire Public Radio reported that the display will continue through the weekend during the peak fall migration period for songbirds. Many songbirds travel at night, and artificial light can attract them or alter their routes. The summit is normally far darker than an urban setting, making the installation’s local effect uncertain.

New Hampshire Audubon has worked with Cornell University scientists, the New York City Bird Alliance, New Hampshire Fish and Game and State Parks on a protocol for switching off the beams if observers see dangerous behavior. During a test earlier in the week, monitors saw birds remain below about 2,000 feet and avoid the new lights.

Observers plan to use binoculars, spotting equipment and a thermal monocular capable of detecting birds and bats. Their weekend watch will help determine whether the memorial can continue safely while migration traffic passes over the White Mountains.
dek: Conservation groups and state agencies have a shutoff protocol as twin memorial beams coincide with peak fall songbird migration.
headline: Bird monitors watch Mount Washington’s September 11 tribute beams
